clues: This town lies in the interior of the state of São Paulo in Brazil. It sits about 119 km from the state capital.
This city is spread out, with few tall blocks packed close. So heat islands almost never form, and the heat stays below 40 in the hottest months.
This town split off from a bigger town nearby to stand on its own in 1964. Its roots go back to the start of the 1900s.
This town has the seventh highest pay per person in Brazil. Its wealth flows from great oil and chemical works in the north.
In the north of this town stands a huge oil refinery. It is one of the biggest chemical hubs in Latin America.
